ylt/40/12.1: At that time did Jesus go on the sabbaths through the corn, and his disciples were hungry, and they began to pluck ears, and to eat,
ylt/40/12.10: and lo, there was a man having the hand withered, and they questioned him, saying, `Is it lawful to heal on the sabbaths?' that they might accuse him.
ylt/40/12.11: And he said to them, `What man shall be of you, who shall have one sheep, and if this may fall on the sabbaths into a ditch, will not lay hold on it and raise <FI>it<Fi> ?
ylt/40/12.12: How much better, therefore, is a man than a sheep? --so that it is lawful on the sabbaths to do good.'
ylt/40/12.13: Then saith he to the man, `Stretch forth thy hand,' and he stretched <FI>it<Fi> forth, and it was restored whole as the other.
ylt/40/12.14: And the Pharisees having gone forth, held a consultation against him, how they might destroy him,
ylt/40/12.15: and Jesus having known, withdrew thence, and there followed him great multitudes, and he healed them all,
ylt/40/12.16: and did charge them that they might not make him manifest,
ylt/40/12.17: that it might be fulfilled that was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
ylt/40/12.18: `Lo, My servant, whom I did choose, My beloved, in whom My soul did delight, I will put My Spirit upon him, and judgment to the nations he shall declare,
ylt/40/12.19: he shall not strive nor cry, nor shall any hear in the broad places his voice,
ylt/40/12.2: and the Pharisees having seen, said to him, `Lo, thy disciples do that which it is not lawful to do on a sabbath.'
ylt/40/12.20: a bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench, till he may put forth judgment to victory,
ylt/40/12.21: and in his name shall nations hope.'
ylt/40/12.22: Then was brought to him a demoniac, blind and dumb, and he healed him, so that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.
ylt/40/12.23: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said, `Is this the Son of David?'
ylt/40/12.24: but the Pharisees having heard, said, `This one doth not cast out demons, except by Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons.'
ylt/40/12.25: And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them, `Every kingdom having been divided against itself is desolated, and no city or house having been divided against itself, doth stand,
ylt/40/12.26: and if the Adversary doth cast out the Adversary, against himself he was divided, how then doth his kingdom stand?
ylt/40/12.27: `And if I, by Beelzeboul, do cast out the demons, your sons--by whom do they cast out? because of this they--they shall be your judges.
ylt/40/12.28: `But if I, by the Spirit of God, do cast out the demons, then come already unto you did the reign of God.
ylt/40/12.29: `Or how is one able to go into the house of the strong man, and to plunder his goods, if first he may not bind the strong man? and then his house he will plunder.
ylt/40/12.3: And he said to them, `Did ye not read what David did, when he was hungry, himself and those with him--
ylt/40/12.30: `He who is not with me is against me, and he who is not gathering with me, doth scatter.
ylt/40/12.31: Because of this I say to you, all sin and evil speaking shall be forgiven to men, but the evil speaking of the Spirit shall not be forgiven to men.
ylt/40/12.32: And whoever may speak a word against the Son of Man it shall be forgiven to him, but whoever may speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in that which is coming.
ylt/40/12.33: `Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree bad, and its fruit bad, for from the fruit is the tree known.
ylt/40/12.34: `Brood of vipers! how are ye able to speak good things--being evil? for out of the abundance of the heart doth the mouth speak.
ylt/40/12.35: The good man out of the good treasure of the heart doth put forth the good things, and the evil man out of the evil treasure doth put forth evil things.
ylt/40/12.36: `And I say to you, that every idle word that men may speak, they shall give for it a reckoning in a day of judgment;
ylt/40/12.37: for from thy words thou shalt be declared righteous, and from thy words thou shalt be declared unrighteous.'
ylt/40/12.38: Then answered certain of the scribes and Pharisees, saying, `Teacher, we will to see a sign from thee.'
ylt/40/12.39: And he answering said to them, `A generation, evil and adulterous, doth seek a sign, and a sign shall not be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet;
ylt/40/12.4: how he went into the house of God, and the loaves of the presentation did eat, which it is not lawful to him to eat, nor to those with him, except to the priests alone?
ylt/40/12.40: for, as Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
ylt/40/12.41: `Men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it, for they reformed at the proclamation of Jonah, and lo, a greater than Jonah here!
ylt/40/12.42: `A queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and lo, a greater than Solomon here!
ylt/40/12.43: `And, when the unclean spirit may go forth from the man, it doth walk through dry places seeking rest, and doth not find;
ylt/40/12.44: then it saith, I will turn back to my house whence I came forth; and having come, it findeth <FI>it<Fi> unoccupied, swept, and adorned:
ylt/40/12.45: then doth it go, and take with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having gone in they dwell there, and the last of that man doth become worse than the first; so shall it be also to this evil generation.'
ylt/40/12.46: And while he was yet speaking to the multitudes, lo, his mother and brethren had stood without, seeking to speak to him,
ylt/40/12.47: and one said to him, `Lo, thy mother and thy brethren do stand without, seeking to speak to thee.'
ylt/40/12.48: And he answering said to him who spake to him, `Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?'
ylt/40/12.49: And having stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, he said, `Lo, my mother and my brethren!
ylt/40/12.5: `Or did ye not read in the Law, that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple do profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
ylt/40/12.50: for whoever may do the will of my Father who is in the heavens, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.'
ylt/40/12.6: and I say to you, that a greater than the temple is here;
ylt/40/12.7: and if ye had known what is: Kindness I will, and not sacrifice--ye had not condemned the blameless,
ylt/40/12.8: for the son of man is lord even of the sabbath.'
ylt/40/12.9: And having departed thence, he went to their synagogue,

ylt/40/6.1: `Take heed your kindness not to do before men, to be seen by them, and if not--reward ye have not from your Father who <FI>is<Fi> in the heavens;
ylt/40/6.10: `Thy reign come: Thy will come to pass, as in heaven also on the earth.
ylt/40/6.12: `And forgive us our debts, as also we forgive our debtors.
ylt/40/6.13: `And mayest Thou not lead us to temptation, but deliver us from the evil, because Thine is the reign, and the power, and the glory--to the ages. Amen.
ylt/40/6.14: `For, if ye may forgive men their trespasses He also will forgive you--your Father who <FI>is<Fi> in the heavens;
ylt/40/6.15: but if ye may not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
ylt/40/6.16: `And when ye may fast, be ye not as the hypocrites, of sour countenances, for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear to men fasting; verily I say to you, that they have their reward.
ylt/40/6.17: `But thou, fasting, anoint thy head, and wash thy face,
ylt/40/6.18: that thou mayest not appear to men fasting, but to thy Father who <FI>is<Fi> in secret, and thy Father, who is seeing in secret, shall reward thee manifestly.
ylt/40/6.19: `Treasure not up to yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust disfigure, and where thieves break through and steal,
ylt/40/6.2: whenever, therefore, thou mayest do kindness, thou mayest not sound a trumpet before thee as the hypocrites do, in the synagogues, and in the streets, that they may have glory from men; verily I say to you--they have their reward!
ylt/40/6.20: but treasure up to yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth disfigure, and where thieves do not break through nor steal,
ylt/40/6.21: for where your treasure is, there will be also your heart.
ylt/40/6.22: `The lamp of the body is the eye, if, therefore, thine eye may be perfect, all thy body shall be enlightened,
ylt/40/6.23: but if thine eye may be evil, all thy body shall be dark; if, therefore, the light that <FI>is<Fi> in thee is darkness--the darkness, how great!
ylt/40/6.24: `None is able to serve two lords, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one, and despise the other; ye are not able to serve God and Mammon.
ylt/40/6.25: `Because of this I say to you, be not anxious for your life, what ye may eat, and what ye may drink, nor for your body, what ye may put on. Is not the life more than the nourishment, and the body than the clothing?
ylt/40/6.26: look to the fowls of the heaven, for they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather into storehouses, and your heavenly Father doth nourish them; are not ye much better than they?
ylt/40/6.27: `And who of you, being anxious, is able to add to his age one cubit?
ylt/40/6.28: and about clothing why are ye anxious? consider well the lilies of the field; how do they grow? they do not labour, nor do they spin;
ylt/40/6.29: and I say to you, that not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these.
ylt/40/6.3: `But thou, doing kindness, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth,
ylt/40/6.30: `And if the herb of the field, that to-day is, and to-morrow is cast to the furnace, God doth so clothe--not much more you, O ye of little faith?
ylt/40/6.31: therefore ye may not be anxious, saying, What may we eat? or, What may we drink? or, What may we put round?
ylt/40/6.32: for all these do the nations seek for, for your heavenly Father doth know that ye have need of all these;
ylt/40/6.33: but seek ye first the reign of God and His righteousness, and all these shall be added to you.
ylt/40/6.34: Be not therefore anxious for the morrow, for the morrow shall be anxious for its own things; sufficient for the day <FI>is<Fi> the evil of it.
ylt/40/6.4: that thy kindness may be in secret, and thy Father who is seeing in secret Himself shall reward thee manifestly.
ylt/40/6.5: `And when thou mayest pray, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites, because they love in the synagogues, and in the corners of the broad places--standing--to pray, that they may be seen of men; verily I say to you, that they have their reward.
ylt/40/6.6: `But thou, when thou mayest pray, go into thy chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who <FI>is<Fi> in secret, and thy Father who is seeing in secret, shall reward thee manifestly.
ylt/40/6.7: `And--praying--ye may not use vain repetitions like the nations, for they think that in their much speaking they shall be heard,
ylt/40/6.8: be ye not therefore like to them, for your Father doth know those things that ye have need of before your asking him;
ylt/40/6.9: thus therefore pray ye: `Our Father who <FI>art<Fi> in the heavens! hallowed be Thy name.

ylt/45/5.1: Having been declared righteous, then, by faith, we have peace toward God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
ylt/45/5.10: for if, being enemies, we have been reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved in his life.
ylt/45/5.11: And not only <FI>so<Fi> , but we are also boasting in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom now we did receive the reconciliation;
ylt/45/5.12: because of this, even as through one man the sin did enter into the world, and through the sin the death; and thus to all men the death did pass through, for that all did sin;
ylt/45/5.13: for till law sin was in the world: and sin is not reckoned when there is not law;
ylt/45/5.14: but the death did reign from Adam till Moses, even upon those not having sinned in the likeness of Adam's transgression, who is a type of him who is coming.
ylt/45/5.15: But, not as the offence so also <FI>is<Fi> the free gift; for if by the offence of the one the many did die, much more did the grace of God, and the free gift in grace of the one man Jesus Christ, abound to the many;
ylt/45/5.16: and not as through one who did sin <FI>is<Fi> the free gift, for the judgment indeed <FI>is<Fi> of one to condemnation, but the gift <FI>is<Fi> of many offences to a declaration of `Righteous,'
ylt/45/5.17: for if by the offence of the one the death did reign through the one, much more those, who the abundance of the grace and of the free gift of the righteousness are receiving, in life shall reign through the one--Jesus Christ.
ylt/45/5.18: So, then, as through one offence to all men <FI>it is<Fi> to condemnation, so also through one declaration of `Righteous' <FI>it is<Fi> to all men to justification of life;
ylt/45/5.19: for as through the disobedience of the one man, the many were constituted sinners: so also through the obedience of the one, shall the many be constituted righteous.
ylt/45/5.2: through whom also we have the access by the faith into this grace in which we have stood, and we boast on the hope of the glory of God.
ylt/45/5.20: And law came in, that the offence might abound, and where the sin did abound, the grace did overabound,
ylt/45/5.21: that even as the sin did reign in the death, so also the grace may reign, through righteousness, to life age-during, through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ylt/45/5.3: And not only <FI>so<Fi> , but we also boast in the tribulations, knowing that the tribulation doth work endurance;
ylt/45/5.4: and the endurance, experience; and the experience, hope;
ylt/45/5.5: and the hope doth not make ashamed, because the love of God hath been poured forth in our hearts through the Holy Spirit that hath been given to us.
ylt/45/5.6: For in our being still ailing, Christ in due time did die for the impious;
ylt/45/5.7: for scarcely for a righteous man will any one die, for for the good man perhaps some one also doth dare to die;
ylt/45/5.8: and God doth commend His own love to us, that, in our being still sinners, Christ did die for us;
ylt/45/5.9: much more, then, having been declared righteous now in his blood, we shall be saved through him from the wrath;

ylt/60/1.1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the choice sojourners of the dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
ylt/60/1.10: concerning which salvation seek out and search out did prophets who concerning the grace toward you did prophecy,
ylt/60/1.11: searching in regard to what or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ that was in them was manifesting, testifying beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glory after these,
ylt/60/1.12: to whom it was revealed, that not to themselves, but to us they were ministering these, which now were told to you (through those who did proclaim good news to you,) in the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, to which things messengers do desire to bend looking.
ylt/60/1.13: Wherefore having girded up the loins of your mind, being sober, hope perfectly upon the grace that is being brought to you in the revelation of Jesus Christ,
ylt/60/1.14: as obedient children, not fashioning yourselves to the former desires in your ignorance,
ylt/60/1.15: but according as He who did call you <FI>is<Fi> holy, ye also, become holy in all behaviour,
ylt/60/1.16: because it hath been written, `Become ye holy, because I am holy;'
ylt/60/1.17: and if on the Father ye do call, who without acceptance of persons is judging according to the work of each, in fear the time of your sojourn pass ye,
ylt/60/1.18: having known that, not with corruptible things--silver or gold--were ye redeemed from your foolish behaviour delivered by fathers,
ylt/60/1.19: but with precious blood, as of a lamb unblemished and unspotted--Christ's--
ylt/60/1.2: according to a foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, to obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace be multiplied!
ylt/60/1.20: foreknown, indeed, before the foundation of the world, and manifested in the last times because of you,
ylt/60/1.21: who through him do believe in God, who did raise out of the dead, and glory to him did give, so that your faith and hope may be in God.
ylt/60/1.22: Your souls having purified in the obedience of the truth through the Spirit to brotherly love unfeigned, out of a pure heart one another love ye earnestly,
ylt/60/1.23: being begotten again, not out of seed corruptible, but incorruptible, through a word of God--living and remaining--to the age;
ylt/60/1.24: because all flesh <FI>is<Fi> as grass, and all glory of man as flower of grass; wither did the grass, and the flower of it fell away,
ylt/60/1.25: and the saying of the Lord doth remain--to the age; and this is the saying that was proclaimed good news to you.
ylt/60/1.3: Blessed <FI>is<Fi> the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to the abundance of His kindness did beget us again to a living hope, through the rising again of Jesus Christ out of the dead,
ylt/60/1.4: to an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and unfading, reserved in the heavens for you,
ylt/60/1.5: who, in the power of God are being guarded, through faith, unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time,
ylt/60/1.6: in which ye are glad, a little now, if it be necessary, being made to sorrow in manifold trials,
ylt/60/1.7: that the proof of your faith--much more precious than of gold that is perishing, and through fire being approved--may be found to praise, and honour, and glory, in the revelation of Jesus Christ,
ylt/60/1.8: whom, not having seen, ye love, in whom, now not seeing and believing, ye are glad with joy unspeakable and glorified,
ylt/60/1.9: receiving the end of your faith--salvation of souls;
